veranderings.voor: Steek die prop in die muur en die ketel maak
veranderings.na: Steek die prop in die muur, en die ketel maak
veranderings.rede: The second clause has its own subject and verb (die ketel maak), so AWS 2017 puts a comma before en.

veranderings.voor: die draadjies in die stof los
veranderings.na: die draadjies in die materiaal los
veranderings.rede: For a Grade 4 learner 'stof' first means dust; 'materiaal' is the clear everyday word for the fabric being ironed.
Same reason as above, and keeps the two mentions of the fabric consistent.

veranderings.blok: Nie alles kom uit as die deel wat ons wil hê nie
veranderings.voor: Dit gaan meestal as hitte weg waar
veranderings.na: Dit beland meestal as hitte waar
veranderings.rede: 'gaan weg' straight after 'raak nie weg nie' reads as a contradiction; 'beland' keeps the meaning without the clash.

vlae.blok: Wat in elkeen gaan en wat uitkom
vlae.teks: Die motor en die fiets: petrol, diesel of die ryer se energie gaan in, en beweging kom uit.
vlae.rede: Read literally, 'die ryer se energie' can attach to the motor as well as the bicycle; the pairing (petrol/diesel for the car, the rider for the bicycle) is only implied. Not changed, because splitting it would change the list item's content.

vlae.teks: Die strykyster kry sy energie deur 'n draad uit die muur. Sy uitset is hitte, en die hitte maak die draadjies in die stof los.
vlae.rede: 'draad' (the electric cord) and 'draadjies' (the fibres of the fabric) sit in adjacent sentences for two different things, which may confuse a Grade 4 reader. A different word for the fibres would be a vocabulary decision for the writer, so it is flagged, not changed.
